page: Amazon Web Services c5n.18xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the Nitro hypervisor. It features 72 vCPUs and 36 physical cores powered by an Intel Xeon 8124M processor running at 3.4 GHz. The x86_64 architecture includes 192.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, yielding 2.67 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage.

A defining feature of the c5n.18xlarge is its baseline network bandwidth of 100 Gbps, designed for network-intensive workloads. Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core CPU performance, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 66660.83 and a PassMark CPU extended instructions test score of 65810.62. Memory read bandwidth is also strong, reaching 3704.68 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 208.32 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

While multi-core and memory read capabilities are strong, single-core execution remains average, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1191.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1425.49. Large block memory write speeds (90.55 GB/sec) and LLM text generation speeds (such as 7.23 tokens/sec for a 7B model) are relatively weak. Consequently, this instance is suited for network-bound compute workloads, database operations, and multi-threaded applications rather than memory-write-heavy or LLM text generation tasks.
